CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/21/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 989236
Permit API: 117-22132
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's OMR well site in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 3/21/2023 at 1040. The weather was 39 degrees and sunny. The site was concluding flow-back operations at the time of inspection. An Act 9 sign was observed at the entrance. There were nine wells onsite capable of production and tagged with appropriate identifiers. Areas surrounding the pad remain stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover or rock cover. There was no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation leaving the site at the time of inspection. Post-Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls remain onsite. Temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls remain in place. Temporary storage tanks onsite were observed in secondary containment nearly full with stormwater (picture 5). The DEP recommends disposing of this stormwater appropriately to assure this containment has the proper volume for spill capture.Excavated remedial areas from a production fluid release on 11/29/2022 remain covered with plastic (pictures 7 and 8). Stormwater retained in the bio-retention basin and draining from this basin's outlet pipe was field measured for a conductivity range below 200 uS/cm. Puddles observed on the pad surface were field measured for a conductivity range between 845- 453 uS/cm. Water observed in the rock line channel running along the pad edge beneath the remediation areas was field measured for a conductivity of 183 uS/cm. There was no evidence of any new spills/releases at the time of this inspection. Violations cited against API #117-22132 on 11/30/2022 remain outstanding at this time. The DEP departed the site at 1200.

properties.content:

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8180427
Permit API: 125-22753
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/12/2024
Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On 03/21/2025 the DEP received a spill/release on the pad surface notification (CTS #387689) from representative Steve Moyer. Steve stated "they noticed a stain about 45' x 25' next to the wellheads off containment on gravel. The conductivity was high. Estimating about 1 to 1.5 barrels of produced water was released. An environmental consultant was contacted who will scrape up material." On 03/24/2025 at 0750 hours the DEP spoke with representative Steve Moyer. He stated that there was a leak within the secondary containment that led to this release. A crew scraped the material on 03/21/2025. New gravel has be placed in the 45' x 25' reported release area (photo #2). Upon further investigation it was determined that a crew had been onsite pumping brine down a well to stop the flow to be able to change the wellhead master valve. After they completed work and the area began to dry out a crystal staining was observed. On 03/24/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection for Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) STETHERS Location Well Pad in Wyalusing Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and cloudy. I arrived at 0940 hours. A representative onsite stated the recovered material from the 03/21/2025 release was removed from the site the same day. Recovered material from the 01/29/2025 discovered release (Inspection Report #3907635 and 3919693) was also being removed from the site on 03/21/2025 and continued to be removed during the incident response inspection report on 03/24/2025 (photo #10).Due to the quantity of the release this is being referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance. Violations against API #015-23923 (Inspection Report #3907635 and 3919693, Enforcement ID 437898) remain open:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection at the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 8/1/2019 @1050 hours. The weather was 72 degrees and sunny. Present onsite for the inspection were myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consultant, Scott West, JKLM. JKLM called the Department's spill line, at 0515 hours the same day, to report a release of approximately 42 gallons of stimulation fluid. The report stated, during ongoing completion activities a water line separated from the well head spraying the fluid mostly onto containment, with a portion depositing on the pad surface. As of today's inspection, Whipper Hill Consulting was present onsite screening the SW corner of the well pad just off containment. Ms. Tokarz stated a vac truck had removed all fluid on the pad surface from the release. Ms. Tokarz was completing a grid survey of soil conductivity readings on the impacted pad surface in preparation for removing the impacted pad material into onsite waste containers. Elevated conductivity fluid was observed inside the pad containment and was being removed with a vac truck. JKLM stated the surrounding E&S controls were screened and found not to be impacted. JKLM estimated the volume of fluid released to the pad surface was >5 gallons but less that 1 barrel. The DEP received confirmation from JKLM the impacted material has been removed and soil conductivity readings, in the impacted area, are <1.5mS/cm. The spill has been remediated. Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 3HU, API#105-21924: 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a) SWMA 301 CSL 402(b) We departed the site at 1230 hours.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well.This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, the well's API number is displayed on the jack. A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl stock tank and a plastic brine tank within an earthen containment is located beside the well. There is evidence of heavy deer activity inside and outside of the containment in the vicinity of the brine tank. Specific conductance (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment is near 1000 uS/cm and the SPC of the soil on the exterior of the containment berm is also elevated (~800 uS/cm). This indicates that the fluid released inside the containment has seeped through the containment wall. Water in the ditch just outside of the containment also has elevated SPC (~ 1300 uS/cm). The elevated SPC readings were detected in an approximate 3' x 10' section of the ditch that also has signs of heavy deer activity. There is no apparent impact to the ditch beyond where the deer tracks are present, as SPC concentrations of the water quickly return to background levels.There is currently a minimal amount of fluid in the brine tank, there are no structural issues apparent with the tank or plumbing. I contacted TJ Allshouse and he agreed to an upcoming field meeting to further investigate the matter.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery to contain fluid inside of it will also need to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Comments: On 5/2/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Wesley Sammons who described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. The crew was currently drilling the production section on the 75HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,444 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,743 feet. After this well, there are two more to follow with this rig drilling just the production sections. The surface and intermediate sections were previously drilled by a different rig. Wes expects it to take until approximately 6/24/2024 for the rig to finish at the site.Wes accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open-top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board. During a previous inspection I witnessed elevated conductance water along the north perimeter berm. I did not witness water in this area during this inspection. Following up on a previous inspection, I collected water sample 9551-108 from the sediment basin near the center overflow inlet box and water sample 9551109 from within the outlet pipe at the corresponding drain grate. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. Vegetation is becoming established in recently constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berms 2 and 3 and the sedimentation basin do not yet meet the vegetative requirements for permanent stabilization.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Prevent water with elevated levels of aluminum from leaving the pad surface, from entering the sediment basin, from leaving the LOD and from infiltrating into the groundwater. 2. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 3. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.4. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.5. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1110 hours.

The GPU secondary containment has been repaired, with no holes or tears observed during this inspection (Photo 3 and 4). The secondary containment of the production tanks and GPU units are holding a small amount rainwater at the time of inspection. However, this appears to be from todays rainfall (Photos 3, 4, and 6). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on the well pad surface during this inspection.Based on todays inspection, the violation issued in IR 4230485 for failure to post the operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) will remain outstanding. Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of approximately 10 gallons of reclaimed stormwater occurred to the pad surface on December 20, 2025. A drilling rig remains in operation on the well pad. I met with Repsol representative Harry Lammy upon arriving on location. He accompanied me during this inspection and showed me the location of the release to the pad surface. According to Mr. Lammy, no fluid absorbed into the pad material since the ground was frozen at the time of the release. He also stated that the pad surface would be screened again for electrical conductivity following drilling operations to ensure that the pad material was not impacted by the release. The fluid released was stormwater which had been collected from the well site secondary containment, he also said. The impacted area of the pad surface was frozen during this inspection so that soil electrical conductivity readings could not be taken. Four GPUs have been installed on the well pad within secondary containment. Violations noted and are considered immediately corrected.

Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/30/2024
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 8185717
Permit API: 003-22651
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/30/2024
Comments: On April 30, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resource's Drape James Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued: 3/29/23 and expires: 3/28/28) located in Frazer Township, Allegheny County in response to CTS #380249.Nick Reda of Range Resources reportedly noticed on April 30, 2024 at 8:15AM an approximately 84 gallon release of water based drill mud on the graveled well pad in several areas. Nick notified the emergency hotline by 10:02AM and believes there is likely one or more holes in the secondary containment causing fluid to leech out from under the containment.The findings of this inspection are as follows: Upon walking the well pad, orange spray paint markings were made by Nick to designate the affected areas plus some buffer space since it was starting to rain. 7 distinct designated areas were observed, some areas had puddles of fluid in them while other areas had stained gravel. Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. These readings subjugate that a release has in fact occurred, that the areas marked by Nick are the contaminated areas, and that at the time of the inspection the release had not appeared to seep past the visibly marked contaminated areas. The perimeter of the well site on the side of the pad where the release occurred was walked and 2 key way drains were investigated. Both drains were dry and soil conductivity readings were taken at each one (0.091 mS and 0.027 mS). Based on these conductivity readings and the lack of fluid coming from the drains, it does not appear that at this time, the release has seeped down into the drainage system.While onsite, SPSI arrived to begin the remediation process. A skid steer was observed scraping up contaminated gravel into piles, a vacuum truck and 2 clamshell roll off dumpsters were scheduled to arrive today and once they do, the truck will suck up all contaminated fluids and the skid steer will pick up all reachable contaminated gravel/sediment and place it in the dumpsters for disposal. Nick stated that Range was not sure on an exact area in which the release originated from. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release and promptly find and repair any holes or tears in the secondary containment to prevent any further releases. The Department also requests the Operator notify the Department of any further releases or impacts that occur and supply the Department with secondary containment inspection reports within 2 business days of receipt of this report.

Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Violation ID: 8252370
Permit API: 129-28299
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/16/2025
Comments: On October 16 2025, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Uschak 2 Well Pad and associated wells.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.At the time of inspection, the well pad had 5 total wells, all of which appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the 1H well head at the time of this inspection. Upon inspection of the 1H well head, the Department observed fluid actively leaking from the well head. The fluid appeared to be leaking from the handwheel on the wellhead. Stained and saturated gravel was observed beneath the well head in an area about 1 foot in diameter. A conductivity reading was taken of the fluid from the source of the leak on the handwheel with a reading of 14.00mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the stained and saturated gravel below the wellhead with readings of 2.81mS, 2.30mS, 4.64mS, 5.25mS. These readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading of 0.20mS.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke to operator representative Brad Campbell via phone call and informed him of the observed leak. Mr. Campbell stated they would assess and ensure the leak is fix/remediated.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested for further evaluation of the well head and the observed corrosion.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.
